content: These methods have been used and expanded to analyze pernicious, but often implicit social biases BIBREF23. For example, BIBREF8 analyzed racial bias in police transcripts by training machine learning classifiers with linguistic features informed by politeness theory BIBREF8, and BIBREF24 investigated historical racial biases in mass media through changing word embeddings BIBREF24. Other work has looked at words in particular syntactic contexts to analyze power and agency, and how these concepts relate to gender bias in movies BIBREF25 and in mass media articles about the #MeToo movement BIBREF26. There has also been a growing focus on the analysis of subtle manifestations of social biases, such as condescension BIBREF27, microagressions BIBREF9, and “othering" language BIBREF28, BIBREF29. In addition, our focus on dehumanization is closely related to the detection and analysis of hate speech and abusive language BIBREF30, BIBREF31.
